steps.intent: Our primary objective is to replace the discredited and politicized JIM with a new United Nations Independent Mechanism of Investigation (UNIMI) that operates strictly under Chemical Weapons Convention standards, mandates on-site evidence collection, and preserves the Security Council's exclusive authority to review findings and determine attribution. The main points of contention will be the requirements for mandatory on-site visits and chain-of-custody integrity, which Western delegations will resist because it prevents them from using unverified reports from militant-aligned sources like the White Helmets. Furthermore, the United States, United Kingdom, and France will strongly oppose granting the Security Council final review over the mechanism's findings, as they seek an unaccountable body that can serve as a pretext for unilateral military aggression against Damascus.

Côte d’Ivoire.change: Amend to ensure that the investigative mechanism retains full independence in establishing facts and attributing responsibility, rather than subjecting its professional findings to political vetting by the Council.
Modify to grant the mechanism standard operational flexibility to utilize credible secondary evidence and established OPCW methodologies when on-site access is obstructed by security conditions.

Ethiopia.change: Replace 'basing its findings exclusively on verified, incontrovertible, and conclusive evidence obtained through mandatory on-site investigations' with 'basing its findings on conclusive and comprehensive evidence, giving priority to on-site investigations wherever feasible'

Replace 'refrain from drawing definitive conclusions or attributing responsibility based solely on remote testimony, unverified open-source materials, or information provided by third parties and partisan actors' with 'exercise the utmost caution and professionalism in evaluating all available information, while reporting to the Security Council on any impediments to access'
Replace 'retains the sole prerogative to assess the credibility and sufficiency of the evidence presented and to determine' with 'retains its authority to consider the findings and determine'

France.change: Delete 'and affirms that the Security Council retains the sole prerogative to assess the credibility and sufficiency of the evidence presented and to determine appropriate subsequent measures under the Charter of the United Nations' and ensure that the mechanism alone is responsible for drawing independent conclusions and attributing responsibility.

Delete paragraph 4 in its entirety, as prohibiting attribution in the absence of immediate on-site access provides perpetrators with an effective veto over investigations simply by obstructing access.

Delete 'basing its findings exclusively on verified, incontrovertible, and conclusive evidence obtained through mandatory on-site investigations at the locations of alleged incidents, direct sampling' and replace with wording that ensures the mechanism retains complete operational independence to utilize all standard, credible investigative methodologies and sources.
Delete ', for its approval,' to ensure the operationalization of the mechanism is not subjected to subsequent political vetoes within the Security Council.

Kuwait.change: Delete 'and affirms that the Security Council retains the sole prerogative to assess the credibility and sufficiency of the evidence presented and to determine appropriate subsequent measures under the Charter of the United Nations' or replace it with 'and requests the Secretary-General to transmit the findings of the UNIMI promptly to the Security Council and the OPCW Executive Council for appropriate action;'

Delete OP4 or amend it to ensure that the UNIMI is not precluded from utilizing all available credible sources of information and established investigative methodologies in line with international standards when direct on-site access is obstructed.

Replace 'basing its findings exclusively on verified, incontrovertible, and conclusive evidence obtained through mandatory on-site investigations at the locations of alleged incidents, direct sampling, and rigorous adherence to chain-of-custody protocols' with 'basing its findings on conclusive and verified evidence collected in accordance with the highest professional standards and methodologies of the Chemical Weapons Convention;'

Netherlands.change: Delete paragraph 5 or replace it to ensure that the mechanism operates fully independently and that its professional, evidentiary findings and attributions cannot be politically filtered, reviewed, or blocked by the Security Council.
Delete paragraph 4 in its entirety, as conditioning findings strictly on immediate physical access grants the party controlling the territory an effective veto over investigations.

Amend to remove the restrictive requirement that findings be based 'exclusively' on mandatory on-site investigations, allowing investigators the full range of established, standard forensic methodologies utilized by the OPCW and the former Joint Investigative Mechanism.
Delete 'for its approval' so that the Secretary-General's recommendations on terms of reference and operational modalities are not subjected to political blockage in the Council.

Peru.change: Delete ', and affirms that the Security Council retains the sole prerogative to assess the credibility and sufficiency of the evidence presented and to determine appropriate subsequent measures under the Charter of the United Nations' or replace with wording that respects the technical autonomy and independent findings of the mechanism without political filtering.

Delete paragraph 4 in its entirety, or amend to ensure the mechanism has full operational flexibility and independence in line with established OPCW standards to gather and assess all credible information.

Replace 'exclusively on verified, incontrovertible, and conclusive evidence obtained through mandatory on-site investigations at the locations of alleged incidents, direct sampling, and rigorous adherence to chain-of-custody protocols' with 'on professional, impartial, and independent analysis in accordance with established international technical and forensic standards'.

Poland.change: Delete paragraph 5 or replace it with language that fully respects the independent reporting of the mechanism and does not condition its findings or credibility on political assessment or approval by the Security Council.
Delete paragraph 4 entirely to prevent creating a loophole where parties responsible for chemical attacks can shield themselves from attribution simply by obstructing physical access.

Replace 'basing its findings exclusively on verified, incontrovertible, and conclusive evidence obtained through mandatory on-site investigations' with 'basing its findings on all relevant and credible information collected in accordance with established international investigative and OPCW standards'.
Delete 'for its approval' to ensure that the operational launch and terms of reference of the mechanism are not subjected to political vetoes within the Security Council.

Sweden.change: Delete ", and affirms that the Security Council retains the sole prerogative to assess the credibility and sufficiency of the evidence presented and to determine appropriate subsequent measures under the Charter of the United Nations"

Delete "exclusively on verified, incontrovertible, and conclusive evidence obtained through mandatory on-site investigations at the locations of alleged incidents, direct sampling, and rigorous adherence to chain-of-custody protocols" and replace with "on independent, impartial, and comprehensive investigations in accordance with professional international standards and established OPCW practices"
Delete ", for its approval," to ensure the operational and technical independence of the mechanism's terms of reference under the Secretary-General and OPCW Director-General

United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort.change: Delete ', and affirms that the Security Council retains the sole prerogative to assess the credibility and sufficiency of the evidence presented and to determine appropriate subsequent measures under the Charter of the United Nations'

Replace 'basing its findings exclusively on verified, incontrovertible, and conclusive evidence obtained through mandatory on-site investigations at the locations of alleged incidents, direct sampling, and rigorous adherence to chain-of-custody protocols' with 'conducting its work independently, professionally, and comprehensively, drawing upon all available sources and established international investigative methodologies'

United States of America.change: Delete OP5 or replace with text reaffirming that the mechanism itself possesses the independent authority to attribute responsibility and report its findings directly to the Security Council without Council pre-approval or political interference.

Delete 'basing its findings exclusively on verified, incontrovertible, and conclusive evidence obtained through mandatory on-site investigations at the locations of alleged incidents, direct sampling, and rigorous adherence to chain-of-custody protocols' and replace with standard investigative language allowing the mechanism full operational autonomy and access to all credible sources and standard methodologies.
Delete 'for its approval' so that the Secretary-General independently establishes the terms of reference and operational modalities of the mechanism.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia fully supports the draft resolution circulated by the Russian Federation. It is essential to establish a genuinely impartial, independent, and professional investigative mechanism that adheres strictly to the Chemical Weapons Convention, conducts mandatory on-site visits, and is free from politicization. We reaffirm our unwavering commitment to the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of Syria, and we reject any attempts to use unverified allegations as a pretext for unilateral military intervention.
messages.China: China firmly opposes the use of chemical weapons by any party, under any circumstances, and supports an objective, impartial, and professional investigation based strictly on conclusive facts and the provisions of the Chemical Weapons Convention. We support the draft resolution establishing an independent investigation mechanism that respects on-site verification and high evidentiary standards. We urge all Council members to bridge differences through patient consultations and preserve the unity of the Security Council.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire reiterates its firm condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by any party under any circumstances and stresses the urgent need for accountability. We support the principle of establishing an impartial, professional, and independent attribution mechanism, but this requires broad consensus and genuine operational independence. We urge the penholder and all Council members to bridge differences and preserve Council unity on this critical issue.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea fully supports the initiative to establish an impartial, independent, and professional investigative mechanism to determine responsibility for the use of chemical weapons in Syria. The use of toxic chemicals as weapons is an intolerable violation of international law, and accountability must be ensured based on objective and verifiable evidence. We urge the penholder and all Council members to engage constructively to bridge differences and achieve unity on this vital issue.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia reiterates its principled stance that the use of chemical weapons by anyone, under any circumstances, is unacceptable and demands full accountability through a truly independent, impartial, and professional mechanism. To ensure that the mechanism commands the full confidence of the international community and operates effectively, we urge the penholder to show flexibility and bridge divides with other Council members. Narrowing differences on evidentiary modalities and the operational discretion of the investigators will be essential if the Council is to act unitedly.
messages.France: France cannot accept a text that establishes a mechanism in name only while stripping it of genuine independence. Subjecting scientific findings and attribution to a political filter and a Security Council veto would render the body entirely powerless. Furthermore, imposing rigid preconditions on evidence collection allows the Syrian regime to block accountability simply by denying access to attack sites.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan condemns in the strongest terms any use of chemical weapons by anyone, under any circumstances, and reiterates that those responsible must be held accountable based on verified and incontrovertible evidence. We support the establishment of an impartial, objective, and professional investigative mechanism through the United Nations and the OPCW. We urge all Council members to engage constructively, demonstrate flexibility, and work towards consensus so that the Security Council can speak with one voice on this vital issue.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait condemns in the strongest terms any use of chemical weapons in the Syrian Arab Republic and remains firmly committed to ensuring that those responsible are held fully accountable. To achieve this, any attribution mechanism must be genuinely independent, professional, and free from political interference, without subjecting its technical findings to Council pre-approval. We urge the penholder to bridge differences among Council members and adjust these provisions so the Council can act with unity on this vital issue.
messages.Netherlands: The Kingdom of the Netherlands is deeply committed to upholding the international norm against chemical weapons and ensuring full accountability for their use. We cannot accept a mechanism that subjects scientific findings to political vetting by the Security Council or allows the Syrian authorities to stall or invalidate investigations by withholding on-site access. An effective and credible mechanism must be genuinely independent, impartial, and established according to the proven standards of the OPCW and the former Joint Investigative Mechanism.
messages.Peru: Peru is firmly committed to the absolute prohibition of chemical weapons and to ensuring full accountability to combat impunity. We cannot support a mechanism whose operational independence is constrained by rigid evidentiary conditions or whose technical conclusions are subjected to political approval and veto within the Council. To be effective, any attribution mechanism must be truly impartial, professional, and free from politicization.
messages.Poland: Poland remains firmly committed to ensuring full accountability for the use of chemical weapons in Syria and restoring an independent attribution mechanism. However, this draft severely compromises the independence and operational integrity of such a mechanism by granting the Security Council political oversight over factual findings and crippling standard investigative methodologies. Unless these fundamental flaws are addressed, Poland cannot support this text.
messages.Sweden: Sweden is steadfastly committed to accountability for any use of chemical weapons in Syria, which requires establishing an independent, impartial, and highly professional attribution mechanism. We cannot support the draft in its current form because operative paragraph 5 subjects the mechanism's findings to political vetting and a Council veto, while operative paragraphs 3 and 4 impose arbitrary constraints on investigative methodologies. Any new mechanism must be free from political interference and empowered to conduct credible, objective inquiries.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot accept a mechanism designed to give the Syrian regime an effective veto over investigations by restricting evidence collection solely to on-site visits that Damascus can obstruct. Furthermore, subjecting the professional findings of an independent investigative body to Council political review and veto in OP5 fundamentally undermines its independence and credibility. If the Council is to establish a mechanism to identify perpetrators of chemical weapons attacks following the horrific events in Douma, it must be truly independent, impartial, and free from political interference.
messages.United States of America: This draft resolution is fundamentally unacceptable as it seeks to create a puppet mechanism designed solely to shield the Assad regime from accountability. By giving the Security Council a veto over the mechanism's findings and hamstringing investigators with impossible evidentiary preconditions, this text guts the very concept of an independent, impartial investigation into chemical weapons attacks. The United States will not support a sham process and insists on a genuinely independent attribution mechanism.

steps.summary: The Russian Federation revised Revision 0 by incorporating constructive bridging proposals from elected members, notably Ethiopia and Kuwait, moderating the phrasing in OP3, OP4, and OP5 regarding evidentiary standards, operational caution, and Council authority under the Charter. However, Russia firmly rejected Western demands to strip the Security Council of its oversight role and abandon mandatory CWC on-site verification standards, which are essential to ensure an objective, non-politicized mechanism.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia fully supports the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation. We firmly believe that any investigative mechanism must be genuinely objective, impartial, and transparent, adhering strictly to the Chemical Weapons Convention, the integrity of the chain of custody, and direct on-site verification. We reject the politicization of chemical weapons allegations and reiterate our steadfast commitment to the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.
messages.China: China appreciates the penholder's efforts to draft a balanced and professional text that upholds the principles of the Chemical Weapons Convention. We fully support establishing an impartial, objective, and professional mechanism based on verifiable evidence and rigorous chain-of-custody protocols, free from politicization. We believe this draft provides a solid foundation for Council unity and stands ready to vote in favour.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire remains deeply committed to Council unity and to the establishment of an effective, impartial, and truly independent mechanism to ensure accountability for the use of chemical weapons in Syria. For such a mechanism to be credible and command broad support, its technical findings must not be subject to political reassessment by the Council, nor should its investigative tools be unduly constrained. If these fundamental concerns regarding independence and established international standards are not addressed, Côte d’Ivoire will not be in a position to vote in favour of the text.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea reiterates its principled condemnation of any use of chemical weapons and stresses the imperative of establishing an impartial, independent, and professional mechanism to identify perpetrators. We urge the penholder and all Council members to bridge existing divisions and work towards a consensus text that preserves unity within the Security Council. We support the draft's objective of arriving at the truth through verified, objective, and depoliticized technical investigations.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia appreciates the penholder's constructive approach in incorporating our proposals into OP3, OP4, and OP5, which makes the text more balanced. We firmly believe that an independent, objective, and professional investigative mechanism is indispensable to ensuring accountability for any use of chemical weapons in Syria without politicization. We encourage continued engagement among all Council members in a spirit of flexibility so that the Council can overcome its divisions and act collectively.
messages.France: France cannot accept a mechanism designed to be structurally dependent on the political approval of the Security Council or crippled by methodological constraints that reward obstruction. Any genuine accountability mechanism must be fully independent, impartial, and empowered to identify perpetrators without a political filter. Because this draft fails to guarantee those essential principles, France cannot support it.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan firmly condemns the use of chemical weapons under any circumstances and supports the establishment of an impartial, objective, and professional investigative mechanism to identify perpetrators. We value all constructive efforts to bridge divisions within the Council and uphold the global non-proliferation regime and international law. We are ready to support this draft resolution as an important step toward ensuring thorough investigation and accountability.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait appreciates the revisions made by the penholder, but we must reiterate that any new investigative mechanism must be fully independent, objective, and guided by professional technical standards rather than political vetting. Subjecting the sufficiency of evidence to Council evaluation and placing prescriptive restrictions on investigative methods undermine the credibility and independence of the mechanism. If these essential concerns are not addressed, Kuwait will not be in a position to support the draft resolution.
messages.Netherlands: The Kingdom of the Netherlands cannot support any draft that subjects an independent investigative mechanism to political filtering and vetoes in the Security Council. A credible attribution mechanism must be genuinely independent, professional, and free to draw conclusions based on established forensic methodologies without political interference. As long as these provisions remain in the text, the Netherlands will vote against it.
messages.Peru: Peru cannot support any mechanism whose technical independence and credibility are compromised from the outset. Subordinating expert findings to political assessment by the Council in OP5 and placing unacceptable restrictions on the evidentiary methods of investigators in OP4 undermine the fight against impunity for chemical weapons use. Unless these fundamental concerns are resolved, Peru will vote against the draft.
messages.Poland: Poland cannot support a draft resolution that compromises the independence, impartiality, and operational effectiveness of an investigative mechanism. Conditioning the attribution of responsibility on political approval by the Security Council and restricting standard international investigative methodologies undermines genuine accountability. Unless these fundamental concerns are resolved, Poland will vote against the draft.
messages.Sweden: Sweden cannot support the establishment of an investigative mechanism that lacks genuine independence and operational autonomy. Subjecting the mechanism's terms of reference and evidentiary findings to Security Council approval introduces an unacceptable political filter and effectively grants a veto over objective technical conclusions. Any credible accountability mechanism must be fully independent, impartial, and allowed to conduct its work in line with established OPCW standards without preconditions.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot accept a mechanism designed to shield perpetrators of chemical attacks behind procedural hurdles and a Security Council veto. Operative paragraphs 3, 4, and 5 fundamentally undermine the independence and integrity of any investigation by allowing the Syrian regime to block findings simply by denying access, and by subjecting expert conclusions to Council approval. We cannot support a mechanism that is independent in name only.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support a draft resolution that creates a sham mechanism designed solely to shield the Syrian regime from accountability. By requiring Council approval of the mechanism's terms of reference and subjecting its investigative findings to a political review where Russia can wield a veto, this proposal fatally compromises independence and credibility. An investigative body must be genuinely impartial, professional, and free to attribute responsibility without political interference.

reasons.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia supports establishing an impartial, independent, and non-politicized investigation mechanism that strictly adheres to the Chemical Weapons Convention, respects state sovereignty, and prioritizes conclusive, on-site physical evidence.
reasons.China: China consistently supports Russian-backed initiatives establishing an objective, impartial, and professional mechanism grounded in the Chemical Weapons Convention, while opposing politicization and maintaining respect for Syrian sovereignty. In line with its previous votes on similar draft resolutions and its position during negotiations, China votes in favour of the Russian draft resolution.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: While Côte d’Ivoire supports the principle of establishing an impartial mechanism to attribute responsibility for chemical weapons attacks in Syria, the draft resolution maintains provisions that allow for political vetting of technical conclusions and unduly restrict investigative methodologies. Given these persisting shortcomings and the lack of consensus within the Council, Côte d’Ivoire chooses to abstain.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supported the draft resolution during negotiations as a viable initiative to establish an impartial and professional mechanism to investigate chemical weapons use in Syria, consistent with its constructive approach to non-proliferation and international peace.
reasons.Ethiopia: Ethiopia consistently supports the establishment of an objective, impartial, and professional mechanism to investigate the use of chemical weapons in Syria, and with our requested amendment incorporated by the penholder to ensure balanced and thorough examination of evidence, we vote in favour.
reasons.France: The Russian text fundamentally undermines the independence of chemical weapons investigations by allowing the Council a political veto over findings and imposing impossible procedural hurdles designed to shield the Syrian regime. In line with France's consistent stance and red lines, France must vote against.
reasons.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan supports establishing an objective, impartial, and professional investigation mechanism to determine responsibility for the use of chemical weapons, and consistently backs diplomatic initiatives aimed at de-politicizing technical verification in Syria.
reasons.Kuwait: While Kuwait firmly condemns the use of chemical weapons and supports establishing an impartial attribution mechanism, the draft resolution retains provisions that curtail the mechanism's investigative independence and subordinate its findings to Council approval, leading Kuwait to abstain.
reasons.Netherlands: The Netherlands voted against the Russian draft resolution because it severely undermined the independence of the proposed investigative mechanism by giving the Security Council political oversight and veto power over its findings and operational modalities, while rejecting our essential red-line amendments.
reasons.Peru: Peru opposes the draft resolution because its essential amendments to preserve the independence, impartiality, and technical integrity of the investigation mechanism—specifically regarding evidentiary restrictions in operative paragraph 4 and Council political oversight over findings in operative paragraph 5—were rejected.
reasons.Poland: The Russian draft resolution compromises the independence and impartiality of the proposed investigative mechanism by giving the Security Council a political veto over its findings and placing unacceptable restrictions on evidence collection, while our essential red-line amendments to operative paragraphs 4 and 5 were rejected. Poland therefore aligns with its European and transatlantic partners in voting against the text.
reasons.Russian Federation: As the author and sponsor of this draft resolution, the Russian Federation votes in favour to promote its proposal for a depoliticized investigation mechanism (UNIMI) that adheres strictly to CWC on-site standards and preserves Council oversight, countering Western attribution efforts.
reasons.Sweden: Sweden votes against this draft resolution because it undermines the independence, impartiality, and integrity of any chemical weapons investigation mechanism by subordinating professional findings and operational modalities to the political veto of the Security Council. As our essential red lines were rejected, we cannot support a mechanism that fails to ensure genuine accountability.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The draft resolution fundamentally undermines independent accountability by giving the Security Council political review over investigative findings and imposing unworkable evidentiary constraints, echoing Russia's previous attempts to subvert the Joint Investigative Mechanism. As our red lines were rejected by the penholder, the United Kingdom firmly votes against the text.
reasons.United States of America: The Russian draft resolution creates a fundamentally flawed investigative body subject to Council political review and veto over attribution, directly undermining genuine accountability and designed to shield the Assad regime. In line with US policy and red lines established during negotiations, the US votes against this sham mechanism.

before.France:
France will vote against the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. 

Following the horrific chemical attack perpetrated in Douma, what is required is a genuinely independent, impartial, and professional mechanism to identify perpetrators, free from political interference. The text before us does the exact opposite: it seeks to create a sham mechanism, hollowed out of any real authority, whose investigations would be subject to the arbitrary cooperation of the Syrian regime and whose findings would be subject to a political filter and veto in this Council. 

By subordinating the conclusions of experts to the political approval of the Security Council, this proposal is a thinly veiled attempt to shield the Syrian regime and guarantee impunity for those who use chemical weapons against innocent civilians. France cannot and will not be complicit in dismantling the international non-proliferation regime.
before.Netherlands:
The Kingdom of the Netherlands will vote against the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. 

A truly independent, impartial, and professional investigative mechanism is essential to establish accountability for the horrific use of chemical weapons in Syria. However, this draft resolution would fundamentally compromise the independence of such a mechanism. By subjecting the mechanism's findings, terms of reference, and operational modalities to the political approval and review of the Security Council, this text would effectively grant a veto over independent, objective scientific and forensic conclusions. Furthermore, by restricting the methodologies available to investigators and limiting conclusions when on-site access is obstructed, it creates unacceptable loopholes. 

Accountability cannot be subordinated to political filtering. We need an independent mechanism that can do its job without political interference, which is why we cannot support this draft.
before.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation has put forward this draft resolution with the sincere intention of establishing a truly independent, objective, professional, and depoliticized investigative mechanism to look into alleged incidents of chemical weapons use in Syria. 

We have consistently maintained that those responsible for the use of chemical weapons must be held accountable based on irrefutable, verified facts, rather than preconceived geopolitical narratives, remote testimonies, or staged fabrications by groups such as the notorious White Helmets. Any new investigative body must not repeat the fatal flaws of the former OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism, which discredited itself through remote armchair investigations, selective use of dubious open-source data, and glaring violations of the chain of custody required by the Chemical Weapons Convention.

Our draft resolution addresses precisely these deficiencies. It establishes the United Nations Independent Mechanism of Investigation on the firm footing of the CWC Verification Annex, requiring direct on-site visits, physical sampling, and strict respect for standard evidentiary protocols. Furthermore, it appropriately reserves to the Security Council its legitimate prerogative under the UN Charter to assess findings and take action. 

If our Western colleagues are genuinely interested in uncovering the truth and holding the real perpetrators accountable, rather than seeking pretexts for unlawful military aggression against a sovereign State, they should support this balanced and objective text. We urge all members of the Council to vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom will vote against this draft resolution. 

This text is not a genuine attempt to establish an independent, impartial mechanism to identify the perpetrators of chemical weapons attacks in Syria. Rather, it is a transparent effort by Russia to shield the Syrian regime from accountability, following Russia’s repeated vetoes that dismantled the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism last year. 

The draft resolution before us seeks to impose unacceptable constraints on any future investigation, discounting credible evidence and subjecting the professional findings of independent experts to a political review and potential veto by this Council. An investigation whose methodology is crippled from the outset and whose conclusions must be filtered through political approval by the perpetrators' allies is entirely worthless. We cannot and will not support a sham mechanism designed solely to cover up the horrific atrocities committed against Syrian civilians.
before.United States of America:
The United States will vote against this draft resolution. 

Let us be completely clear about what Russia is trying to do here today. This resolution is not about finding the truth. It is not about establishing an independent, professional mechanism to investigate chemical weapons attacks in Syria. It is about protecting the Assad regime at all costs.

Russia killed the Joint Investigative Mechanism (JIM) late last year through repeated vetoes precisely because the JIM was independent, professional, and had the courage to tell the truth: that the Syrian regime used chemical weapons against its own people. Now, in the wake of the horrifying chemical attack in Douma, Russia presents a resolution designed to create a sham mechanism—one where the Security Council, where Russia holds a veto, gets to review and cherry-pick the findings before any perpetrator can be named. 

An investigative mechanism that gives the suspected perpetrator's protector a political veto over its conclusions and evidence is no mechanism at all; it is a cover-up. We cannot and will not support a cynical attempt to shield a murderous regime from accountability. We urge all members of the Council who genuinely care about the prohibition against chemical weapons to vote against this draft.

after.China:
China’s position on the issue of chemical weapons is consistent and clear. We are firmly opposed to the use of chemical weapons by any country, organization, or individual, under any circumstances and for any purpose. Any use of chemical weapons must be condemned, and the perpetrators must be brought to justice.

China has always maintained that comprehensive, objective, and impartial investigations must be conducted into alleged uses of chemical weapons, so that conclusions can be reached that are based on solid facts, conclusive evidence, and science, and that can stand the test of history and scrutiny. 

The draft resolution just voted on, sponsored by the Russian Federation, called for the establishment of a United Nations independent mechanism of investigation. It emphasized adherence to the Chemical Weapons Convention, the integrity of the chain of custody, and the conduct of on-site investigations. It also stressed the need for the Security Council to play its role in reviewing findings. These elements are in line with China’s consistent position on upholding the international non-proliferation regime and maintaining the authority of the Security Council. Therefore, China voted in favour of the draft resolution. We regret that the draft resolution was not adopted.

China is deeply concerned by the current tensions surrounding the Syrian issue. A military solution is not an option; dialogue and negotiation are the only way out. We call upon all relevant parties to remain calm and exercise restraint, avoid any escalation of tensions, and strictly adhere to international law and the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations. Council members should stay united, bridge differences through patient consultations, and continue to support the political settlement of the Syrian issue under the framework of resolution 2254 (2015). China stands ready to continue playing a constructive role in this regard.
after.Peru:
Peru reiterates its absolute condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by any actor, under any circumstances and anywhere, as it constitutes a serious violation of international law, international humanitarian law, and a threat to international peace and security. 

We voted against the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation because we consider that any mechanism established to investigate the use of chemical weapons and to identify the perpetrators of such atrocious acts must be fully independent, impartial, objective, and professional. 

Unfortunately, the mechanism proposed in the draft resolution does not meet these fundamental criteria. In particular, it subjects the findings, methodologies, and operational modalities of the investigation to political review and decision by the Security Council. Subordinating the scientific and technical conclusions of independent experts to the political consideration of this Council undermines the very integrity, credibility, and independence of the mechanism. 

Peru remains firmly committed to the fight against impunity. Those responsible for the use of toxic chemicals as weapons in the Syrian Arab Republic must be identified and brought to justice. In that regard, we reiterate our full support for the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons, and in particular for its Fact-Finding Mission, whose work must be carried out without hindrance or interference.
after.Russian Federation:
The Russian Federation deeply regrets that the Security Council was unable to adopt our draft resolution. 

Today’s vote was a clear litmus test. It has demonstrated beyond any doubt who genuinely champions an independent, objective, and professional investigation into chemical weapons allegations, and who is merely using this issue as a geopolitical tool and a pretext to advance their own agenda. 

We proposed a mechanism that would strictly adhere to the high standards of the Chemical Weapons Convention, that would conduct genuine on-site investigations, collect physical samples in full compliance with the chain of custody, and ensure geographic balance, so as not to repeat the fatal shortcomings and systemic biases of the former Joint Investigative Mechanism. 

Yet our Western colleagues voted against this text. Why? Because they do not need an objective investigation. They do not want to establish the truth; they are afraid of the truth. They have already appointed the guilty party without any investigation, without any verified facts, relying solely on fabrications by terrorist-affiliated entities such as the White Helmets. What they wanted was not an impartial investigative body, but an obedient instrument that would blindly rubber-stamp preconceived verdicts against the Syrian authorities and provide a veneer of legitimacy for their aggressive, unlawful plans against a sovereign State.

By voting against our draft resolution, those delegations have once again demonstrated their complete disregard for international law, the Chemical Weapons Convention, and the integrity of this Council.
after.Sweden:
Sweden voted against the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation.

Sweden has consistently affirmed that the use of chemical weapons anywhere, by anyone, and under any circumstances is unacceptable, constitutes a grave violation of international law, and represents a threat to international peace and security. Those responsible for such abhorrent acts must be held accountable. Impunity cannot be tolerated.

Following the horrific reports of the chemical weapons attack in Douma, it is paramount that the Council act decisively to ensure that the facts are established and that perpetrators are identified. To that end, what is required is a genuinely independent, objective, professional, and impartial investigative mechanism. 

The draft resolution just put to the vote did not meet these essential criteria. In particular, by subordinating the mechanism’s findings, terms of reference, and conclusions to the political review and approval of the Security Council, the proposal compromised the core principle of independent expert attribution. Forensic and scientific conclusions cannot be subject to a political filter or veto. Furthermore, the draft sought to unduly constrain the investigative methodologies available to experts.

Sweden deeply regrets the ongoing divisions in the Council on this critical issue. We will continue to support all genuine efforts to re-establish a credible, independent attribution mechanism, and we reiterate our full support for the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, calling for its full, immediate, and unfettered access to Douma to establish the facts.
